body: I think we should try to use data from https://github.com/Z-Anatomy/Models-of-human-anatomy, if we didn't already. So we can reproduce the precise acoustically affecting part of mouth and breathing organs.
We also need to try rebuilding 3D model based on research at https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12440228
We also should try to use https://github.com/diku-dk/Open-Full-Jaw for maximum detail model, we always can scale down from maximum detailed model.

We also need to integrate the most accurate data from https://humanatlas.io, for example https://apps.humanatlas.io/kg-explorer/ref-organ/mouth-male/v1.0

We should slice our 3D model as MRI does, if we have reference MRI, and we should be able to compare key points automatically when possible.

If the source of models already in 3D, we should incorporate all of them to increase quality, and make configurable flexible simulator that allows to switch between all variations between gathered 3D models by configuration of any part of them.

Meaning we should generalize.

We may also need to use ideas from meta human (Unreal Engine) and other formats.

And we should have head only adapter demoes for these, like we did in https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar (yet there the voice generation and voice animation was done completely wrong).

We should be able to have automated bridges to different formats of character models to simulate correctly talking animation, that is actually anatomically correct.

So by providing best possible level of detail as the basis and carefully scale it down to multiple simplier levels, we should be able to have GPU optimized simulation of sound on high end GPUs and simple yet working acoustic and animation simulation on less powerful GPUs and CPUs.

Also check we fully deliver on:
- https://github.com/konard/voice-simulator/pull/10#issuecomment-6248419847
- https://github.com/konard/voice-simulator/pull/10#issuecomment-6248312336
- https://github.com/konard/voice-simulator/pull/10#issuecomment-6248264362

Replies to the review comments. Each one is delivered in this PR, with the details in the [case study](https://github.com/konard/voice-simulator/blob/issue-9-9c7431a3d213/docs/case-studies/issue-9/README.md#review-comments).

**[Z-Anatomy](https://github.com/konard/voice-simulator/pull/10#issuecomment-6248264362)**

- `node scripts/fetch-anatomy.mjs z-anatomy DIR` downloads the atlas just in time.
- `scripts/blender/z_anatomy_export.py` copies only the mouth, pharynx and larynx objects out of its `.blend` and writes them as STL. The file is opened with `--factory-startup --disable-autoexec`, so the scripts bundled with the atlas never run.
- `zAnatomySource` makes its teeth, bony palate, soft palate, tongue and larynx a source that any part of the model can come from (`npm run export:model -- --atlas z-anatomy=DIR --anatomy z-anatomy`).
- `node scripts/compare-hra.mjs --atlas z-anatomy --dir DIR` slices the model against it. The RMS over the fitted key points is 2.37 mm. Image (CC BY-SA 4.0): [z-anatomy-male-slices.png](https://github.com/konard/voice-simulator/blob/issue-9-9c7431a3d213/docs/case-studies/issue-9/anatomy/z-anatomy-male-slices.png?raw=true).
- Z-Anatomy is built on BodyParts3D, which is a source too (`bodyParts3dSource`, RMS 2.40 mm). The two are the same Visible Human male, so they count as one sample.

**[G-OBIM (PMC12440228)](https://github.com/konard/voice-simulator/pull/10#issuecomment-6248312336)**

- The jaw opens per phoneme as G-OBIM measured on MRI (`src/articulation/teeth.js`, `tests/teeth.test.js`).
- The character rigs take their jaw angle from the same data.

**[Open-Full-Jaw](https://github.com/konard/voice-simulator/pull/10#issuecomment-6248419847)**

- The 17 patients are fetched at run time. The teeth sit on a beta-function arch fitted to their scans, with crown widths and thicknesses from the same scans.
- The dataset is CC BY-NC-SA, so only the statistics are committed, as numbers.
- Each detailed source is reduced from full resolution to every LOD by vertex clustering (`clusterVertices`).

**[HuBMAP atlas and the rest](https://github.com/konard/voice-simulator/pull/10#issuecomment-6250686218)**

- **Organs:** `fetchHra` reads the HuBMAP Visible Human mouth and larynx of both sexes from the remote GLBs with range requests.
- **MRI-like slicing:** `scripts/compare-hra.mjs` cuts the model and the organs midsagittally, parasagittally, coronally and axially, finds ten key points on both automatically and compares them (`compareKeyPoints`, `tests/reference-anatomy.test.js`).
- **Switching parts between sources:** every part (upper and lower teeth, tongue, palate, velum) can come from the procedural model, `hra-male`, `hra-female`, `z-anatomy`, `bodyparts3d` or any glTF (`anatomySourceFromGlb`). Each part is fitted onto the model's dental key points and carried by the jaw (`headModel(head, { anatomy })`, `npm run export:model -- --anatomy ...`).
- **MetaHuman and other formats:** `visemeTrack` produces ARKit blendshapes (the 52 curves used by MetaHuman and Ready Player Me), VRM 1.0 expressions and Oculus visemes. It is available in the library, the CLI (`visemes`) and the server (`GET /api/visemes`).
- **Automated rig bridges:** `bindRig` reads the morph target names of any model and binds whichever convention it uses:
  - ARKit, MetaHuman `CTRL_expressions_*` and Ready Player Me;
  - Oculus and VRChat visemes;
  - VRM 1.0 and 0.x;
  - VRoid `Fcl_MTH_*`;
  - MMD.

  `characterTrack` gives a whole utterance as weights per morph target.
- **Head-only adapter demo, after konard/anime-avatar:** the app's **Talking character** panel drives a procedural face, or any `.vrm`, `.glb` or `.gltf` the user loads, from the same articulation the solvers hear. See [poses.png](https://github.com/konard/voice-simulator/blob/issue-9-9c7431a3d213/docs/case-studies/issue-9/character/poses.png?raw=true) and [app-panel.png](https://github.com/konard/voice-simulator/blob/issue-9-9c7431a3d213/docs/case-studies/issue-9/character/app-panel.png?raw=true).
- **LOD for GPUs and CPUs:** four mesh LODs, and seven audio tiers from a 22-section waveguide to 0.4 cm voxels. The 3D solver runs on WebGPU when there is an adapter and on WASM workers otherwise.
- **Full delivery of the other comments:** checked. The requirements table in the PR description maps every requirement and comment (R1 to R12, C1 to C4) to its code and tests. R9 (beating neural TTS) is reported as partly done. Issue 5 item #25, the YouTube video, is reported as blocked, because YouTube's bot check refuses this environment.
